Maintenance record — 30 October 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Purpose and acceptance criteria

Exact combat probabilities, simulation and interactive play for a documented Risk conquest variant.

The current milestone requires correct supported rules, bounded/validated inputs, meaningful failure-path regressions, an installable source package, and a working local app. Original checkouts and unrelated work are preserved in isolated review branches. No release, push or deployment is implied by this local record.

Evidence-led findings and repairs

  • High: R/turn.R allowed conquest occupation with fewer armies than the dice used in the final attack. Recover that count from final casualties and require the official minimum while retaining one army at the source. Independent one-, two- and three-dice boundary cases protect the rule.
  • Medium: shared numeric checks and reinforcement/fortification arithmetic accepted non-finite values or overflowed. Validate whole counts and bounds before mutation/coercion; preserve the input game.
  • Documentation: explicitly list the omitted cards, missions and printed two-player neutral setup rather than imply a complete official rules implementation.

Rule source checked: https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Risk_World_Conquest_Game.pdf

Roadmap and completion

  1. Essential repairs: correct the confirmed rule/process defects above and protect them with independent boundary cases. Implemented and locally validated.
  2. Everyday use: preserve user state, validate invalid inputs, install the package, exercise play/analysis and the app. Completed for the paths below.
  3. Release preparation: synchronize documentation and package checks. Local candidate prepared; platform CI and maintainer publication review remain.
  4. Deferred enhancements: retain the focused supported model; do not add engines, rule variants or infrastructure without an explicit use case and validation.

Actual verification

R 4.6.1 on ARM64 macOS, 30 October 2026:

  • Full source tests: 631 assertions passed. Full packaged tests with vignettes: 623 assertions, 6 conditional skips, no failures. That check reported one namespace note for tail; qualified it as utils::tail and reran packaging/checks Status OK with --no-tests after the complete passing suite above.
  • Installed journey: all 42 territories, 60 legal actions, army accounting, and independently enumerated 15/36 one-die odds passed.
  • Installed browser app: map/reset, 3-vs-2 duel table, battle histogram (100 simulations) and strategy comparison (2 games, 5 rounds) passed with no page errors.

Exact command results and logs are retained locally in /Users/rh/Documents/GitHub/.repository-audit/2026-10-30-rheller-refinement/risikoR/. Failures preceding fixes remain there alongside the final evidence.

First use from this checkout

Install R (tested with 4.6.1). For compiled dependencies use Xcode command-line tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows, or the matching Linux C/C++ toolchain. From this repository, install dependencies and the local candidate:

Rscript --vanilla -e 'install.packages("remotes", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org"); remotes::install_local(".", dependencies=TRUE, upgrade="never", build_vignettes=FALSE)'
Rscript --vanilla -e 'risikoR::rk_run_app()'

Open the local URL printed by Shiny. The README gives the scriptable workflow. To repeat source tests, run Rscript --vanilla -e 'pkgload::load_all(); testthat::test_local(stop_on_failure=TRUE)' after installing the development dependencies.

Limits and next release action

The whole-game model is a conquest variant. Card trading, secret missions and the printed two-player neutral setup are deferred; they require an explicit rules-design milestone. Native Windows/Linux and hosted CI were not run.

Review the local diff and run required platform CI on the chosen release commit; then decide whether to publish. No hosted result or external acceptance is claimed.
